proposal.original_claim_summary: The entry attributes a broad multi-year FBI purge to Kash Patel beginning at his February 2025 confirmation and combines pre-Patel DOJ actions, later Patel-era firings, staffing claims, lawsuits and other investigations.

identified_problems.explanation: The record merges several distinct episodes: January 2025 DOJ-directed personnel reviews before Patel became FBI director, August 2025 firings of senior FBI officials under Patel, and February 2026 firings of at least a dozen agents tied to Trump investigations.

The accepted sources support repeated firings of named officials and agents connected to January 6 or Trump-related investigations, but not the stored claim that Patel had fired 'hundreds of agents deemed insufficiently loyal'.
The January 31, 2025 review and firings predated Patel's confirmation and therefore cannot accurately be described as actions he oversaw as FBI director.

frozen_original.title: Kash Patel Purges FBI of Agents Who Investigated Trump
frozen_original.synopsis: After being confirmed as FBI Director in February 2025, Kash Patel oversaw the firing of hundreds of agents deemed insufficiently loyal to President Trump, including agents assigned to the January 6 investigation and the classified documents case. In January 2025, Trump posted on Truth Social demanding Patel fire 'total scum' FBI agents after reading a right-wing article; Patel confirmed the agents had already been terminated. By August 2026, the bureau faced a staffing crisis with an exodus of hundreds of experienced counterterrorism officials. Two fired agents sued Patel and AG Bondi in March 2025 alleging First and Fifth Amendment violations. Patel moved to cut the FBI Office of General Counsel — the body responsible for ensuring lawful investigations — by 25 percent, with Axios reporting in August 2025 that the FBI had opened investigations into multiple people on Patel's pre-confirmation 'deep state' list, including former CIA Director John Brennan and former FBI Director James Comey.

proposal.original_claim_summary: The entry says Trump repeatedly promised throughout July 2025 that a 'historic, perfect' Iran nuclear agreement was imminent, but talks completely collapsed by month's end.

identified_problems.explanation: No credible contemporaneous source located supports the quoted 'historic, perfect' imminent-deal sequence in July 2025.

Reuters reported on July 14 that no date or location had been set for resuming U.S.-Iran nuclear talks following the June war. That supports stalled diplomacy, not the specific stored promise-and-collapse narrative.
The phrase 'perfect deal' appears in later 2026 conflict reporting and should not be backdated into July 2025 without evidence.

proposal.proposed_synopsis: The record should be hidden or rebuilt around documented July 2025 diplomacy. Reuters reported on July 14 that Iran and the United States had not set a date or location to resume nuclear talks after the June conflict, while G7 governments urged negotiations to restart. The reviewed evidence does not substantiate the entry's repeated 'historic, perfect deal is imminent' quotations or a discrete end-of-July collapse event.

frozen_original.title: Trump's Promised Iran Deal Fails to Materialize
frozen_original.synopsis: Throughout July 2025, Trump repeatedly claimed that a 'historic, perfect' new nuclear deal with Iran was imminent. However, by the end of the month, negotiations had completely broken down, with Iranian officials denying any serious talks were even taking place. The administration's diplomatic bluff severely undermined U.S. credibility on the global stage.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Pam Bondi DOJ Drops All Pending Cases Against Trump Allies on Day One
proposal.original_synopsis: On January 20, 2025, within hours of her confirmation as Attorney General, Pam Bondi directed the DOJ to drop all pending federal cases against Trump associates and allies, including cases that had been brought by career prosecutors following the January 6 investigation and other matters. The mass dismissal of cases bypassed normal DOJ review processes and was carried out without explanation of the merits. Career DOJ prosecutors who had worked the cases for years described the action as politically motivated and legally unjustifiable. The move was characterized by former officials as an unprecedented purge of legitimate prosecutions for purely political purposes, effectively ending DOJ independence as a check on presidential power.

frozen_original.title: Trump Ends WIC Formula Assistance for Immigrants
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, the Trump administration issued new guidance barring immigrant families — including those with legal immigration status such as green card holders and visa holders — from participating in the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), which provides formula, food, and nutritional support to low-income pregnant women, new mothers, and infants. WIC had previously been available to immigrants with qualifying immigration status. The policy change particularly impacted immigrant families with U.S.-born citizen children who were now barred from receiving WIC benefits despite their legal status. Pediatricians warned the denial of infant formula assistance posed direct health risks to newborns in low-income immigrant families. Public health researchers projected increased rates of infant malnutrition and low birth weight as a consequence.
